title: Contextuality Evidence Lab: Exact Sequential Certificates and a Constructive Setting-Bias Attack
peer_review_status: Research methods artifact & preprint (not peer reviewed; AI-assisted under human direction)
author: Alexander Stephen Donahue
core_result: Proves a finite adaptive-tree sequential contextuality evidence theorem and a sharp setting-bias bound for the Peres-Mermin square, constructing an explicit classical adversary causing a miscalibrated 1% test to reject 97.24% of the time while the bias-aware test stays below 1%.
verification_boundary: Adaptive-tree evidence bound, biased-setting classical cap (11/12), and counterexample are formally verified in Lean 4; paired with reproducible Moonlab/QGTL/QRNG/Eshkol simulation. Explicitly disclaims hardware contextuality or certified randomness.
